turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, I'm Sister Jacobs. Vitals first, then the doctor will call you. On the scale, please.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, umm, ok. I've been dodging the scale, hey, my jeans are hanging off me and that was already going on before the trip, so the number is going to depress me.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Weight today is fifty-two kilograms. Last time in March you were sixty-eight.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Eish. Ja. I knew it, I just didn't want it said out loud.

[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Your last pressure was one-forty. Temperature thirty-seven point eight, no, sorry, I looked too soon. Thirty-eight point three degrees. Pulse jumped to one hundred and two when the clip slipped, it's actually ninety-four.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I knew I was warm. I feel like a wet rag, like I've overdone it on this whole trip thing.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come in, you can both sit. I'm Doctor Naidoo. What brings you in today?

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): The reason I came is my eyes have gone yellow, and my wee is dark, and I'm exhausted. I need to tell you the whole trip or it won't hang together, sorry, I over-explain when I'm scared.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Over-explain if you need to. Where did you go?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Down the Wild Coast in my cousin's car, four of us, and we ate at the roadside stalls, chicken, pap, vetkoek sitting in the sun, and I even had a second one. Three of the others fell ill too, my cousin was vomiting all the next day. There was a generator and music, I couldn't hear myself think, but ag that's just the noise, not why I'm here.
[SEG0011] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, the yellow has been three weeks, and she's vomiting every morning. I begged her to come and she kept saying just now.

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No, uh, the timing's wrong. I saw the yellow last Thursday, so six days, not three weeks. And it's not every morning with the vomiting. I vomited once, the Tuesday night, and since then it's just queasy, sick in the stomach, I haven't thrown up again.

[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me reflect that. Yellow eyes, you say six days and your carer says three weeks, so about six days to three weeks, and you two don't agree. You vomited once and the rest is nausea, not every morning. Dark urine and exhaustion as well. Fair?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, that's fair. The queasy part comes on after I eat. And the tiredness is every day since we got back, by lunch I'm a wet rag and I have to go lie down, it's awful.
[SEG0015] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Fair on the vomiting, I think I piled it on. The eyes though, I'm not walking the three weeks back. She looked yellow to me before Thursday.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, we'll leave the timing unsettled. Urine and stool, in your own words.

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): The wee is dark like Coke, or rooibos left in the cup, and it started about the day before I noticed the eyes. The stool has gone pale, like clay or putty, which I googled at two in the morning, I know, I google everything and then I panic.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any itching? Were you feverish at home? And alcohol, do you drink?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): My arms itch at night, not terrible, just annoying. I felt hot and shivery the Sunday after that stall food. Alcohol, no, I don't drink, never have, not a sip at Christmas, my dad drank and I swore I wouldn't.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the tummy? And your breathing, any problems there at all?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): The tummy is sore on the right, under the ribs, a dull ache, worse after I eat. Breathing is fine, my chest is completely fine. Also my feet feel dead, both of them, pins and needles since that long drive, and it's still there a bit in the mornings.
[SEG0022] person_4 (CAREGIVER): And she stopped her medicine. The gout tablet, I don't think she's taken it all week.

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I did not stop that one. It's alopurinol, a hundred milligrams every morning, by mouth, for the gout, still taking it, years now. I stopped the Panado, the paracetemol. Two tablets, a thousand milligrams, three times a day, by mouth, for the headache on the trip, and the headache had settled by the Wednesday, and I stopped those tablets on Friday because the wee was dark.

[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): So allopurinol one hundred milligrams every morning, still in use, for gout. Paracetamol one thousand milligrams three times a day, stopped on Friday, and the headache had already settled. Any allergies to medicines or food?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergies. Nothing to tablets, nothing to food, I've never come out in a rash or swollen up. The gout is old, the day hospital started the alopurinol, and it's still ongoing.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any old test results you've been told about?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, last year at the clinic in Gqeberha they did liver bloods, and they said it was borderline. No actual number, just the word borderline, and then nobody phoned me, which still bugs me.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll note that as what you were told, borderline, not as a figure I can see. I'm going to examine you.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): The whites of the eyes are yellow. The skin has a faint yellow tinge. Abdomen is soft, tender under the right ribs. I can't feel any enlarged nodes. Chest is clear.

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it bad? My uncle had a bad liver, but he drank, and I don't. I've also got a frog in my throat from the aircon, and I can't hear myself think with that TV in the waiting room, but my voice is fine, sorry, that's a tangent.

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the throat and the TV, they aren't part of this. Uncle with liver disease, noted, and he drank. My working impression is an acute hepatitis, quite possibly from the food, and I can't exclude hepatitis A because the others on the trip were ill too. Provisional, until the bloods.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Should I give you the hour by hour? Monday we left at five, Tuesday was the stall, Wednesday I was flat on the bed, I can keep going.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): I don't need the hour by hour, thank you. I'm booking liver blood tests and hepatitis serology, they'll take them today. A scan of the tummy only if the bloods don't explain it, and I'm not ordering that now.
[SEG0034] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Can she have something for the fever, doctor?

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): No new medicine today, and stay off the Panado. Rest, fluids, plain food, and nothing herbal from the chemist. Come back in one week for the results. Don't sit at home if you get confused or much more yellow.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): One week, ok. And the bloods are today, ja? My carer came in the taxi with me, so transport is fine, I can stay for them.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Liver bloods and the hepatitis serology are today. The scan stays only if those don't answer it. We'll see you in one week.
[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): Sharp. I'll walk you through to the blood room now.

spec.situation: Person with yellow eyes, dark urine and tiredness after eating at roadside stalls on a trip; others at the trip also ill; alcohol denied; liver blood tests and hepatitis serology planned.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

omissions.text: Weight loss amount is implied by prior documented weights: 52 kg today versus 68 kg in March.
Patient denied any breathing problems/chest symptoms with wording that chest is completely fine.
Right upper abdominal pain was described as a dull ache under the ribs.
Pins and needles in both feet persists a bit in the mornings.
Paracetamol was stopped on Friday because the urine was dark.
Patient denied both medicine and food allergies, specifically no prior rash or swelling.
Past history includes being told last year at a clinic in Gqeberha that liver blood tests were 'borderline', with no numeric result available.
Abdominal exam finding that the abdomen was soft is missing.
There is family history detail that the uncle with liver disease drank alcohol.

Recorded investigation fact is wrong: the prior liver blood tests in Gqeberha were historical results the patient recalled being told were 'borderline', not a completed liver blood test requested by the patient in this encounter.
Doctor advised no new medicine today in response to request for something for fever.
